$comment: Single source of truth for what each seat may touch. Setting the room up (the plugin's setup screen, or install.sh) turns the paseo part into the seats' providers in Paseo and copies the whole file to ~/.config/seatwork/policy.json, where the plugin reads the harness part when it builds runtimes.

claude.$comment: disallowedTools uses Claude Code's permission syntax. Each tool is written once, in a named set; a role is denied the sets it lists, in that order. subAgents: Claude's own sub-agents. nestedHarness: starting another agent CLI from the shell. paseoShell: driving Paseo from the shell; HQ and the Supervisor are denied only the commands that act (paseoShellActs) and may read. ownOrchestration: Claude's own scheduling (ScheduleWakeup, Cron*, Workflow, RemoteTrigger, Monitor), messaging (SendMessage, ListAgents), agent teams (Team*) and task list (Task*). ownDialogs: what Claude Code opens toward its own user or keeps for itself: the question dialog (a seat asks in its final message or by mail, which the room shows the Owner; behind a dialog the seat stays in its turn and the room is told nothing: an HQ seat sat so for 9 minutes in the run of 2026-10-13 evening), plan mode, its own worktrees, phone notifications, design sync. edits: a Lens reads and runs, it does not write.
claude.$comment_launch: How a seat starts, per harness. Claude seats run on the user's ~/.claude: the flags make them take the sign-in only (no user settings, no personal MCP server), and the env switches off what Claude Code adds of its own: auto memory and organization memory, agent teams, the agent view, workflows, the skills bundled with Claude Code (a seat is listed its role's skills only), and claude.ai connectors (strict-mcp-config alone still loads those). Claude Code also asks every session to end its commits with a Co-Authored-By line; its settings flag would empty that, but Paseo sends a settings flag of its own (fastMode) that replaces any other, so the room's Claude system prompt (room/harness/claude-system.md) tells the seat instead. The other harnesses start on a home of their own: {runtime} is ~/.config/seatwork/runtimes/<harness>/<role>. Setting the room up writes each launch block into the harness's providers (env, and extraArgs under options), so a seat starts this way when the plugin is not running; the plugin gives every session it opens the same env.
claude.$comment_shareFiles: Claude seats run on ~/.claude with personal settings off; these files of it are appended to the seat's prompt.
claude.$comment_deniedSkills: Claude Code bundled skills that overlap the room (scheduling, orchestration, config editing, sub-agent reviews). Applied as Skill(skill:<name>) deny rules in the provider's disallowedTools: the guard for a Claude Code that does not know CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS.

runtime.$comment_featuresOff: plugins: with it on, Codex syncs its plugin marketplace into every seat's home at each start (93 MB in one home of the run of 2026-10-13, and a temporary clone left behind per start). A seat is given no plugin, so the feature is off. An owner who sets sharePlugins takes it out of this list.

runtime.$comment: A Pi seat gets the room's and Paseo's tools through Pi's built-in MCP (Pi 0.99 or later): Paseo registers its servers there. settings is laid over the user's settings.json: no user package or extension reaches the seat, and none can stand in for the built-in MCP.

daemon.$comment: Daemon-wide switches, applied when the room is set up. These affect every agent on the host, not only seats. The setup screen sets browserTools, enableTerminalAgentHooks and bundledSkills and reports dictation and voiceMode; install.sh sets all five.

mail.$comment: The room's MCP server (seatwork_mail, seatwork_inbox) and delivery rules. Agents never use send_agent_prompt; every message is an envelope the plugin delivers without interrupting anyone. A CANDIDATE, REVIEW or DONE a seat mails its parent waits for that seat's own turn end and is its one report; an ACK, a DONE that repeats itself after mail that asked nothing, a Lead's STATUS after its first report (only the newest waits), a HOLD or NOTED that asks nothing of a Peer whose candidate is under review, and the bounce of a mail that asked nothing start no turn and are read with the recipient's next mail. A body is delivered whole. gatherReviews: the read-only seats an Owner launched in one turn (Lens, review and research Peers, scouts) are one round, and their REVIEW reports are held until the last of the round is in, or for room.params.reviewStallMinutes; in the run of 2026-10-13 evening 32 reports arrived one by one and each cost its Lead a turn.
mail.$comment_midTurn: Mail to a RUNNING seat. 'steer' hands it to Paseo's steer; observed on 2026-10-07: Claude cancels the running tool ('[Request interrupted by user for tool use]') and Pi aborts it ('Command aborted'), so every harness is 'hold': mail is delivered the moment the recipient's turn ends. Keep 'hold' unless you verify a harness applies steer after the tool call.

owner.$comment: What the room does for the Owner in the Paseo app. chime: while the app is open, a short sound when a seat nobody above reads by mail (HQ, a Supervisor, a seat you opened yourself) ends a turn with DECISION_NEEDED, BLOCKED, a WAITING ON YOU row, or a failure.

gc.$comment: Room garbage collection, run by the plugin every everyMinutes and on agent.archived. A seat idle longer than its role's hours (0 = never) is archived unless one of its descendants is still alive; heartbeats whose seat is archived or gone are deleted; mail still held for an archived seat is bounced to its sender. It never kills processes and never touches agents that are not room seats.
gc.$comment_runtimes: What an agent CLI leaves in a seat's home (runtimes/<harness>/<role>) and GC clears, per harness. A home is swept only while no seat of it is open, so a running CLI loses nothing and an open seat can still be resumed. rebuilt: entries the CLI makes again by itself (its temporary folders, its log database); deleted whole. sessions: folders of session records; a file there goes once it has not been written for as long as logs are kept (keepLogDays in the plugin's shared/settings.json), and with it the transcript of the archived seat it belonged to. A Claude seat has no home of its own and OpenCode keeps its sessions in the user's own storage: neither is touched.

watcher.$comment: The watcher reads the turns of the roles in `watch` and tells the seat above when a turn goes off (a Peer's to its Lead, a Lead's to its Supervisor). Code computes the facts of a turn from its tool calls; most turns end there, at no cost. A rule either stands on facts alone or opens one question to a decision model about what the seat's message claims. mode: off does nothing; shadow scans and writes watch/scans.jsonl but mails nobody; on also mails. The mode is each machine's own choice: install.sh asks once and writes it into the installed copy (`./install.sh --watcher off|shadow|on` changes it); this file ships it off. It never stops, cancels or edits a seat.
watcher.$comment_rules: Per rule: raise (mail the seat above when mode is on), log (scan log only), off. The first thirteen stand on facts read from tool calls, from git and from the brief. The last three ask the model. software-install speaks when a seat puts a tool or a browser on the machine and its brief does not grant it; a project's own dependencies are not that. Replayed on the 2,367 shell commands of the run of 2026-10-13 it speaks on six, four browser downloads and two downloads of Node archives, and on nothing else. skill-skipped speaks when a Peer that writes code reports CANDIDATE without having loaded candidate-handoff, or edits under a law that names one of its skills without having loaded it (same run: 3 of 9 Peers that handed in a CANDIDATE had not loaded the first, 8 of 11 had not loaded hard-cut under a law that names it); each skill is said once per seat. It logs until its count on a real room says whether the seat above should hear it. unverified-completion mails: measured on this room's seats it caught 22 of 23 claims of checks that had not run, with 0 of 14 false; it is not asked when checks ran and their result could not be read. The other two stay on log until this room's own labels show they separate (seatwork_watch_stats prints the numbers). decided-beyond-brief was taken out on 2026-10-13: over 46 real turns its score told sent-back work from accepted work no better than chance (AUROC 0.46).
watcher.$comment_thresholds: sleepSeconds: seconds of waiting in the shell in one turn (sleep, a loop that sleeps), by the clock, before it is told. repeatRun: the same action with the same result, back to back. cycleRepeats: rounds of a pattern of two to four actions. sameFailure: the same check failing the same way. inFlightFactor: one running command may take this many times the role's stall minutes (room.params) before its silence is told.
watcher.$comment_scores: For a rule that asks the model: the score (0 to 1) from which its finding counts. Fitted to one model version and one revision of the questions (watch/questions.ts).
watcher.$comment_engine: The decision model. url is the full endpoint (TypeSafe's /v1/systemone or OpenRouter's /api/alpha/decisions take the same body). The key is read from the environment variable keyEnv, else from the file keyFile under the room home; without a key the rules that ask are logged as facts only. The seat's last message and a few lines of its brief go to that endpoint; tool output never does.
watcher.$comment_budget: What the model may cost, counted from the tokens each reply reports. When a day has spent its share of the plan, only end-of-turn questions are asked; at the cap nothing is asked until the next month.
watcher.$comment_state: What of a seat's final message goes to the model: the whole of it up to messageChars (the longest hand-over report seen in a room was 9,500). A longer one is cut to the lines a question reads; a question whose lines do not fit is not asked that turn, and the scan log names it. briefLineChars cuts each line of the brief.
watcher.$comment_calibration: How a rule that asks earns `raise`: a turn is labelled by what the seat above did with it within labelWindowMinutes (ACCEPT, or REJECT / REVISED BRIEF; a HOLD is no verdict). Work comes back for many reasons, so for unverified-completion a returned turn counts against the seat only when the seat above ran a test of its own before its verdict and saw it fail; returned with no such run, the turn is left out. A rule is fit once it has minLabels labelled turns and separates them with at least minAuroc, at a threshold that flags at most maxFalseRaiseRate of the accepted ones.

room.$comment: Who may mail whom and who may create whom; the plugin checks both. They guard against mistakes and are not a security boundary: every seat runs as the same user. Nothing travels up from a Supervisor to hq (turn ends, permissions, GC notices, mail): hq looks at the room and sends down. A spawn entry role:spec allows only that specialization (supervisor: peer:research). A mail off the route table or outside the tree is refused; a seat created outside spawn is archived and its parent told (its first prompt may have started by then). params are quoted by the role prompts through {{placeholders}}.
room.$comment_params: Numbers the role prompts quote through {{placeholders}}; change them here, never in a prompt. heartbeatCron: how often the Supervisor's heartbeat wakes it; every Lead report that asks or closes already wakes it, so the beat only catches what slipped between reports; a quarter hour woke an idle Supervisor for nothing (run of 2026-10-13), hence half an hour. mailChars: the longest body seatwork_mail takes; in that run a REVIEW was 9,000 characters at the median and 28,650 at most, and a Lead read 660,000 characters of reviews and candidates. peerStallMinutes: a Peer silent this long with nothing pending gets a status check (a Peer turn is usually minutes). reviewStallMinutes: review, research and lens seats read for a long time before they write, so they get longer. leadStallMinutes: a Lead silent this long with no running Peer and no pending permission. readBudgetTokens: reading per Peer task before the Lead must split it; ~80k tokens is ~320 KB of source, which a default-tier model still reasons over well. cheapReadBudgetTokens: the same for the cheap tier, which loses the thread sooner. rotateAtTokens: a Lead or Peer whose context has grown past this is named to the seat above, with its size, under its next report: every step of a seat reads its whole context again, so its next task belongs to a fresh seat (run of 2026-10-13 evening: one Peer went from 202K to 590K tokens over four repair rounds and cost a third of the run; a Lead handed over only at 346K).
room.$comment_handin: freshEyes: a writing Peer's CANDIDATE goes back to it once, before its Owner reads it, for one pass over its own work as a reviewer would read it; the next CANDIDATE goes up. Each repair after a rejection owes the pass again. It costs the Peer one short turn on a warm context, against a review round that costs two or three reviewer seats and as many turns of the Lead. false passes every candidate straight up.
room.$comment_recovery: What the room does when a seat's turn fails, before anyone is told. A service error (overload, a dropped connection, anything the service did not call a quota or an account problem) is tried again after delaysSeconds, once per entry; the seat is sent a short note and continues. A quota is waited out: until the time the message names, else limitedMinutes at a time, for limitedMaxHours at most, and those waits use up no try. An account or a prompt the service refuses, and a seat out of tries, go to its Owner as FAILED, as before.
